name: EFC-R-SPARC
title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
description: A pilot-scale analysis applying Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) to 20 SPARC galaxies spanning diverse morphological types, demonstrating regime-dependent validity where EFC achieves 100% success for LSB and dwarf galaxies but systematically underperforms for barred spirals. Introduces the EFC-R (Regime) framework decomposing total energy as Etotal = Eflow + Elatent to delineate EFC's domain of validity, supported by a statistically significant correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.705, p = 0.0005) between structural complexity and EFC performance.

energy_flow_field.description: Effective energy field in EFC where ρ is local energy density and S ∈ [0,1] is a normalized entropy field

circular_velocity.description: Circular velocity prediction from the energy-flow potential Φ_e

delta_aic.description: Model comparison criterion; negative values favor EFC, positive values favor ΛCDM

energy_decomposition.description: EFC-R energy decomposition separating flow-dominated and latent (structurally complex) contributions

key_results.main_finding: EFC achieves 100% success rate for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies but 0% for barred/disturbed spirals, with a statistically significant Spearman correlation (ρ = 0.705, p = 0.0005) between structural complexity and EFC performance, motivating the regime-dependent EFC-R framework.

sealed_predictions.statement: EFC will achieve ΔAIC ≤ 2 for ≥90% of LSB galaxies in the full SPARC sample (N~175)
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Running EFC fits on the complete SPARC LSB subsample and finding success rate below 90%

sealed_predictions.statement: The Spearman correlation between structural complexity (latent field proxy L) and EFC residuals will remain ρ > 0.5 at p < 0.01 when extended to the full SPARC sample
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Full SPARC analysis showing ρ ≤ 0.5 or p ≥ 0.01 for the complexity-performance correlation

sealed_predictions.statement: Barred and structurally disturbed galaxies will systematically require Elatent > 0 corrections, while equilibrium-dominated systems will have Elatent ≈ 0
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Finding barred spirals that are well-fit by pure EFC without latent field corrections, or LSB galaxies that require substantial Elatent

kill_criteria: KC1: EFC fails for >50% of LSB galaxies in a full SPARC sample (N≥50 LSB systems), destroying the regime-dependent validity pattern
KC2: The Spearman correlation between structural complexity proxy L and EFC fit quality drops below ρ = 0.3 or becomes non-significant (p > 0.05) on independent galaxy samples of N≥50
KC3: A complete SPARC analysis (N~175) shows EFC mean χ²_red systematically exceeds ΛCDM mean χ²_red across all morphological categories including LSB and dwarf galaxies
KC4: The entropy gradient ∇S is found to be unphysical (negative or divergent) for the majority of galaxies where EFC currently succeeds
KC5: Independent hydrodynamical simulations (e.g., FIRE) show no non-equilibrium effects in dwarf galaxy evolution, removing the physical motivation for regime-dependent validity

related_packages.role: Figshare preprint and supplementary data for the EFC-R SPARC pilot study
